research.title: Benchmark of Multimodal Vision-Language Models for Damage Detection
research.venue: LatinX in Computer Vision (LXCV) Workshop · CVPR 2026 · Denver
research.authors: With Mariana Risco Cosavalente and Prof. Claudio Jung (UFRGS)
research.summary: We evaluated CLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2 and FuseLIP for disaster damage detection on CrisisMMD and DamageDataset, comparing contrastive fine-tuning, two-stage few-shot adaptation and multimodal fusion. Combining image and text consistently outperformed either modality alone, and fine-tuning raised SigLIP's F1 from 0.19 to 0.90.

aiWork.intro: I use AI as a working tool every day — at Canvia and in my own projects — with the same discipline as any engineering practice: clear scope, tests and human review before every delivery.

items.title: Coding agents with a controlled workflow
items.text: Claude Code, Codex and Pi on Gentle Shell and Gentle AI, following ODD (Organic Driven Development): explore before changing, subagents to implement and verify, TDD and risk-based review before every commit.

items.title: Persistent memory
items.text: Engram keeps architecture decisions, findings and task state across sessions, so context is never lost between days or projects.

items.title: Environment tailored to real projects
items.text: Custom skills, MCP servers wired to real systems (read-only Oracle, Laravel Boost, container logs, GitLab, CodeGraph) and model selection per task.

items.title: Agent factory on my own VPS
items.text: Unattended issue execution triggered from Telegram (n8n) and nightly batches, with pull requests and CI as quality gates.

items.title: Multi-tenant RAG platform for BCRP
items.problem: Several institutional applications needed reliable search and assistant experiences over thousands of research documents.
items.contribution: At Canvia, I designed, built and improved the platform, including ingestion and indexing, shared tools, configurable chat/search/prompt modules, multimodal ingestion, and daily testing with human review.
items.architecture: Node.js gateway, Python backend, Oracle 23ai, pgvector, Pinecone, Chroma, SQL pipelines to RePEc, and multimodal document processing.
items.result: One platform serving four BCRP applications; its assistant is live on the Research Portal.

items.title: Certilab RAG for calibration certificates
items.problem: Calibration certificates combine structured fields and document content that users need to search, understand and validate.
items.contribution: I designed agentic and adaptive RAG services with structured/semantic search, source citations, access control, query rewriting and answer verification.
items.architecture: LangGraph, FastAPI, Qdrant, OpenAI and MySQL; the adaptive version works over 3,848 indexed vectors from real certificates.
items.result: A certification system with 300+ certificates issued, plus a production-oriented RAG and chatbot foundation.

items.title: Vision-language models for damage detection
items.problem: Disaster damage detection needed a grounded comparison of vision-language models across CrisisMMD and DamageDataset.
items.contribution: I co-authored the evaluation of CLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2 and FuseLIP, comparing contrastive fine-tuning, two-stage few-shot adaptation and multimodal fusion.
items.architecture: Python, PyTorch, CLIP-family models, fine-tuning experiments and multimodal evaluation pipelines.
items.result: Fine-tuning raised SigLIP F1 from 0.19 to 0.90; the paper was presented at the LXCV Workshop at CVPR 2026.
